title: Prevalence, Thresholds, and Subgroup Performance Gaps in Clinical Prediction Models Across Five Public Datasets
description: Clinical prediction models are commonly compared across demographic subgroups, but a raw performance gap is not a fixed property of a model. Observed gaps should prompt investigation of metric choice, prevalence, threshold, sample composition, measured case mix, and uncertainty rather than being treated alone as proof of discrimination, fairness, or equivalence.

paper.title: Prevalence, Thresholds, and Subgroup Performance Gaps in Clinical Prediction Models Across Five Public Datasets

example_outputs.title: Default inputs
example_outputs.summary: With the paper's specification, the Diabetes-130 youngest-minus-oldest sensitivity gap is +0.120 [−0.057, +0.235]; the paper reports +0.104. 19 of 36 alternative analysis choices give a negative gap. Model hyperparameters and variable encodings are this runbook's; the predictor set and age bands follow the paper. No fairness verdict is implied.

inputs.label: Dataset
inputs.description: diabetes130 (UCI Diabetes 130-US Hospitals, 30-day readmission) or cdc_diabetes (UCI CDC Diabetes Health Indicators)

inputs.label: Attribute
inputs.description: sex, age, or race (race: diabetes130 only)

inputs.label: Age bands
inputs.description: Age comparison bands. diabetes130: 10-29 vs 60+ (paper, default), <50 vs 70+, 10-29 vs 80+. cdc_diabetes: 18-44 vs 65+ (default), 18-24 vs 80+, 18-34 vs 70+

inputs.label: Group A
inputs.description: Override first group for sex/race (e.g. Asian, Hispanic, Female). Blank = paper default

inputs.label: Group B
inputs.description: Override reference group (e.g. Caucasian, Male). Blank = paper default

inputs.label: Threshold
inputs.description: train_prevalence (paper), top20 (flag top 20% risk), or a number like 0.3

inputs.label: Target prevalence
inputs.description: Common prevalence for PPV standardization: pooled (paper) or a number like 0.05

inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: auto (paper's 6-family CV selection) or one of logistic, l1_logistic, shallow_tree, random_forest, gradient_boosting, soft_voting

inputs.label: Multiverse
inputs.description: Re-run the estimate across defensible analytic choices (true/false)

inputs.label: Your confusion matrices
inputs.description: Skip the datasets and audit your own model: GroupA:TP,FP,TN,FN; GroupB:TP,FP,TN,FN (e.g. Women:80,40,800,30; Men:120,90,700,25)
